reviews.title: Ordinary AS3 source-class identity and default Object labels
reviews.reason: Bounded coordinator acceptance of the second ordinary source-class identity extension in the existing typed-collections export. The 19:27:45 UTC source snapshot was unchanged when checked after the shared suite. Its recorded source hashes are retained; subsequent unrelated Button registrations in the shared project compiler are excluded. The earlier mathematics/property/reflection review remains a separate historical record.
reviews.limitations: Only ordinary public AS3 source classes rooted in Object and plain records are covered. The supported Class-valued construction path does not establish the Class metaclass or complete AVM2 type objects. Native-derived/AS2 object paths, arbitrary prototype replacement/mutation, constructor-function models and Object() construction are outside this delta. Default locale labeling is not locale-sensitive numeric/date formatting. No original Flash differential or broad current-tree conformance claim. Existing concurrent AS1/Button shared-tree additions are excluded from acceptance. New describeType/getQualifiedClassName behavior for prototype objects is not promoted without a corresponding scenario. Explicit toString/toLocaleString labeling does not establish Flash-equivalent implicit String or concatenation coercion. Native-derived/AS2 prototype behavior is not newly accepted. This review does not claim the pending final Clippy run.

verification.engine: actual exported Rust WASM + browser Canvas
verification.decision: Actual build passed; Rust 140 tests, 91 emitted-script fixtures, shared project workflows 25/25 and 63 web tests passed. The additional shared AS1 workflow is a regression result only, not independent AS1/Button feature acceptance. The ordinary HTML5 export showed identity/math/object/reflection true initially, after two actions (quantity 17, sqrt 4.12, recent Batch 2/Batch 1), and after Restart (quantity 13, sqrt 3.61, Ready/Empty). No runtime errors; existing Arial-not-embedded warning only. No original Flash differential or complete current-tree conformance is claimed. Subsequent unrelated Button compiler edits are excluded from the captured snapshot evidence.

reviewedEntries.scopeNote: Bounded first-class public source-class value: getDefinitionByName(app.Item) assigned to Class and invoked with new constructs an Item, retaining class/constructor/prototype identity. This is ordinary source-class value behavior, not general Class metaclass construction, loaded bytecode or native class conformance.

Ordinary AS3 source classes rooted in Object have an instance-to-class-prototype-to-source-base-prototype chain and bounded inherited Object identity/default-label operations. Plain records preserve authored string-method overrides. Object construction, arbitrary prototype mutation, native-derived and AS2 object models are not accepted by this delta.

Item constructed through a public Class alias inherits constructor===Item. DerivedRecord.prototype owns a nonenumerable constructor===DerivedRecord. Only this ordinary source-class identity path is accepted; prototype writes, constructor functions and native/AS2 constructor semantics are outside the scenario.

Ordinary source-class prototype identities are stable along Item and DerivedRecord/BaseRecord chains. The scenario observes prototype lookup, own nonenumerable constructor, direct/base ancestry and unrelated-class negatives. No prototype replacement or complete dynamic prototype mutation contract is claimed.

Observed on ordinary source-class prototypes: own Item and DerivedRecord prototypes and the BaseRecord ancestor recognize their instances; unrelated Item/BaseRecord pairs return false. No full native/AS2/proxy/custom-prototype conformance is inferred.

Default method on ordinary source Item returns [object Item]; default method on a plain record returns [object Object] without invoking its authored custom toString. An explicit authored toLocaleString override remains callable. This is default Object labeling, not locale-sensitive formatting of arbitrary native objects.

Shared Rust label formatting returns short-name [object Item] and [object DerivedRecord] for ordinary source instances and [class Item] for the class value. A plain-record authored toString returns its custom label and runs once. Numeric/native-derived/AS2 stringification and complete coercion remain separate.

Default Object valueOf returns the same ordinary source Item instance constructed through a Class alias. Primitive unboxing, custom native objects and full AVM2 coercion are not accepted by this bounded identity observation.
